findings.passage: A covered voter voting under this Article shall not be required to include a photocopy of identification described in G.S. 163-166.16(a) or an affidavit as described in G.S. 163-166.16(d)(1), (d)(2), or (d)(3) when submitting a ballot in accordance with this Article.
findings.note: Crawford is named in the sponsor list of HB 278 and the bill appears on her introduced-bills page (https://www.ncleg.gov/Members/IntroducedBills/H/800). It adds G.S. 163-258.21, so a covered military or overseas voter would not have to include a photocopy of ID, or the listed affidavits, when submitting a ballot. It was referred to the House Rules committee on 03/05/2025 and has no further action listed.
subjects: ID with absentee ballot for military and overseas voters

findings.passage: As a gun owner, I believe in common-sense gun laws that keep our communities safe.  Step one in my plan is to ensure that we elect the right people who value life over the right to bear arms.  Step two is to work with my colleagues and the community to develop a plan that does the following: background checks for every gun purchased, close the gun-show loophole for private sales regarding background checks, and do everything we can, including passing legislation, to ensure that guns are stored safely and properly so that they do not get into the hands of the wrong people.
findings.note: Her written answer to Indy Week's 2024 NC House District 66 questionnaire, question 12 (background checks, bump stocks, age limits, assault-style weapons). Date is the page's published date. The passage starts mid-answer; the answer's first sentence is about who holds power in the legislature.
